post.text:

Which one surprised you?

stories.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX's Starmind: up to 1 million AI data-center satellites
stories.summary: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said SpaceX may put up to 1 million AI computing satellites in orbit, powered by the sun. Amazon, in its March petition to deny, had called the plan 'a lofty ambition rather than a real plan'.

predictions.note: The FCC authorized up to 1 million solar-powered AI computing satellites: an approval for orbital data centres at scale, far from a self-growing network.

stories.title: Dario Amodei calls claims he'd surrender human control to AI 'absurd'
stories.summary: In a long post on X, Anthropic's CEO called the suggestion 'absurd' and said 'turning over governance to AI is a bad idea'. On AI that improves itself, he wrote: 'we may want limits on this process'.

predictions.note: Anthropic's CEO suggested limits on AI that improves itself; it is one executive's view, with no negotiations or agreement yet.

stories.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift Amazon's blockade of Meta's Muse shopping agent
stories.summary: According to Fortune, the companies have held multiple rounds of talks that would let Muse connect directly to Amazon's store; Muse users haven't been able to check out on Amazon for two months. Search results and ads are still open issues.

stories.title: The New York Times publishes a guide to talking about AI doom at Thanksgiving
stories.summary: The New York Times ran 'How to Talk With Your Family About A.I. Doom at Thanksgiving', a guide for the holiday table.

stories.title: AI stocks fall for a second straight day as Anthropic dips to $74
stories.summary: AI-linked stocks were hammered for a second straight day on Wednesday, Reuters reported, and Anthropic traded as low as $73.85 shortly after the open, 11% below its $83 IPO price. The Wall Street Journal said stocks pared losses as Anthropic's shares swung higher.

stories.title: JPMorgan sees the S&P 500 at 8,200 by the end of 2027 on the 'AI supercycle'
stories.summary: JPMorgan's Dubravko Lakos-Bujas set an S&P 500 target of 8,200 for the end of 2027, saying AI is 'in its early innings'. It is a forecast.

stories.title: Anthropic's IPO made about 5,100 staff millionaires, on paper
stories.summary: About 5,100 non-founder Anthropic employees, known as 'Ants', became paper millionaires in the company's 19 Nov IPO, CNBC reported; at least 400 are worth more than $100 million on paper.

stories.title: ElevenLabs reportedly in early talks to raise money at a $33 billion valuation
stories.summary: AI voice maker ElevenLabs is in preliminary talks for a 2027 funding round at a $33 billion valuation, according to Bloomberg.

stories.title: GPT-6.2 Astra named the artist of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook in 22 minutes
stories.summary: Historian Mark Humphries says GPT-6.2 Astra identified the vicomte de Chabot as the artist of an unsigned 1808 sketchbook held at Yale's Beinecke library; Chabot's own diary matched the dates.

stories.title: OpenAI says GPT-6.2 designed proteins that bound five targets in lab tests
stories.summary: In lab tests with partner Onava, 35 of 322 GPT-6.2-designed minibinders (10.9%) bound their targets, five proteins linked to cancer and immune disorders; specialist tools such as SolubleMPNN made the sequences.

predictions.note: GPT-6.2 designed protein binders, 35 of 322 of which bound their targets in lab tests: early lab results, far from an approved drug.

stories.title: New York bans AI chatbot toys for five years
stories.summary: Gov. Kathy Hochul signed a bill banning the manufacture, distribution and sale of AI chatbot toys for five years, with fines of $15,000 a day. New York is the second state after California, and the ban takes effect 90 days after signing.

stories.title: EA brings back the late John Motson's voice with AI in EA Sports FC
stories.summary: EA has added a digitally recreated voice of commentator John Motson, who died in 2023, to EA Sports FC from 26 November, with the consent of his son and wife.

stories.title: XPeng shows its Iron humanoid, due to start work as a store assistant in 2027
stories.summary: At its AI Day in Guangzhou, XPeng showed Iron, with 76 degrees of freedom, over 1,500 tactile sensing points and three of its own Turing AI chips. Per XPeng, it trains as a store assistant from Q1 2027, with a public release targeted for Q2 2027.

stories.title: Figure 03 answers Musk's 'move the table' challenge and still finds the apple
stories.summary: After Musk said humanoid demos are staged and a robot would fail if someone moved the table, Figure CEO Brett Adcock shared a 41-second clip in which Figure 03 retrieves the apple after the table is moved, calling it 'zero shot and fully autonomous'.

stories.title: NTT DATA plans a new AI centre in Derry with 200 jobs
stories.summary: NTT DATA is investing about £23 million in a new AI centre in Derry, Northern Ireland, which will create 200 jobs, the BBC reports.

stories.title: University of Sydney honours students must now defend their theses in conversation
stories.summary: Every honours student at the University of Sydney now has to defend their thesis in conversation, as AI makes written work harder to trust, The Guardian reports.

transcript.t: Welcome to the Singularity Daily, Thursday edition.
Here are the last 24 hours in superintelligence, in 3 minutes.
Heads in the clouds? Try space.
SpaceX just got the go-ahead for a million AI satellites.
Rival Amazon had called it a lofty ambition rather than a real plan.
Meanwhile, Anthropic's Dario Amodei says the claim he'd hand our free will to AI is absurd.
His line in the sand? AI that improves itself.
'We may want limits on this process.'
And Amazon, which has blocked Meta's shopping agent Muse, is reportedly talking about letting it in.
Talking AI doom over Thanksgiving dinner?
The New York Times wrote a guide for that.
Now, the money. AI stocks took a beating for a second day, and Anthropic dipped to $74.
Still, JPMorgan expects the S&P 500 to hit 8,200 next year, thanks to AI.
Anthropic's listing also made about 5,100 of its staff millionaires, at least on paper.
And AI voice maker ElevenLabs is reported ly in early talks at a $33 billion value.
A historian asked ChatGPT who drew a sketchbook from 1808.
22 minutes later: a French nobleman.
And OpenAI's model designed new proteins.
In lab tests, 35 of them latched onto their targets.
The catch? New York just banned AI chatbot toys for five years.
And EA brought back the late John Motson's voice with AI, with his family's consent.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
In China, XPeng showed off Iron, a humanoid with over 1,500 touch sensors.
Early next year it starts training as a shop assistant in XPeng's own stores.
Musk says robot demos are often staged.
So Figure moved the table. Its robot still found the apple.
So keep your head in the clouds, by all means.
Just keep your feet on the ground.
Every day, the curve gets a little steeper.
Somehow, the future keeps landing early.
That's one day of news. Imagine what a year looks like.
That's the Singularity Daily for today.
Same time tomorrow?
Want the whole month? Hear more tomorrow night.
